issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, no labels used. The new swap phase only perturbs the current best and re-optimises it with SLSQP. Every result still goes through finalize() and is accepted only if the sum of radii goes up.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. When `cand` is empty the loop does `continue`, but the `while` condition re-checks the clock, so this cannot loop forever. It does waste iterations if no pair qualifies.

Side effect, not a validity problem: until t0_swap_end (0.85 × time_budget from t0) every iteration takes the swap branch. The old remove-and-reinsert move on the smallest circles now gets only the last ~15% of the budget instead of all the time after the initial phase.

The candidate scored 2.636, the same as the incumbent. That is slightly above the 2.635 quoted as best known, but 2.635 is a rounded figure (the known value is about 2.6358), so this is plausible and not suspicious. The incumbent reaches the same value.
z is about 0 because the candidate and incumbent values are equal. With 1 run each the variance cannot be estimated, so z is only nominal. Reject (no improvement) is consistent with the numbers.
